# RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection
## Imaging Overview
The three standard planes are axial (cross-sectional, viewed as if looking up through the leg), coronal (a front-facing, side-to-side view), and sagittal (a side-profile, front-to-back view). Different structures are best seen in different planes; for example, the cruciate ligaments and menisci are well evaluated on sagittal and coronal images, and the patellofemoral cartilage on axial images.

Interpreting a study therefore requires integrating information across multiple series, planes, and slices for the same knee, an inherently three-dimensional task.
